title: Robust Function Calling for LLM Agents Under Interface Drift

paragraphs.en: Tool-augmented language-model agents rely on interface text: tool descriptions, argument schemas, and the candidate tool list shown at inference time. These interfaces often change after deployment even when the underlying tool semantics remain fixed, creating a practical reliability problem for function-calling systems. We study this failure mode as interface drift and evaluate whether a lightweight, training-free repair layer can recover robustness without retraining the base model. Our method, SchemaShield-Lite, combines schema validation, candidate-set retry for missing tool names, and one-shot constrained repair. On Qwen3.5-9B, it raises DICE-300 accuracy from 0.717 0.717 to 0.813 0.813 and BFCL-200 accuracy from 0.580 0.580 to 0.805 0.805 , recovering 19 / 22 19/22 and 33 / 45 33/45 drift-induced failures with no observed repair harms. Naive retry does not explain the gains. Ablations show that candidate-set drift, especially distractor tools, accounts for most observed damage, while description and schema edits alone are less harmful. The results position validation-and-repair as a practical robustness layer for deployed LLM-agent tool use.

paragraphs.en: Modern language-model agents increasingly depend on external tools for retrieval, execution, planning, and actuation. In practice, however, tool use is mediated entirely through text: tool descriptions, parameter schemas, enum values, and candidate tool lists. Recent work shows that these interface details strongly affect tool selection and argument generation even when the tool semantics are unchanged [ 4 , 2 ] . This creates a deployment problem: tool interfaces drift over time as developers rename parameters, revise descriptions, add examples, or expand candidate tool sets.
paragraphs.zh: 现代语言模型智能体越来越依赖外部工具进行检索、执行、规划和操作。 然而在实践中，工具的使用完全通过文本进行中介：包括工具描述、参数模式、枚举值以及候选工具列表。 近期的研究表明，即使工具的语义保持不变，这些接口细节也会显著影响工具的选择和参数的生成 [ 4 , 2 ] 。 这带来了一个部署问题：随着开发者重命名参数、修订描述、添加示例或扩展候选工具集，工具接口会随时间推移而发生变化。

paragraphs.en: We study this problem as interface drift : benign, semantics-preserving changes to tool interfaces that occur after deployment. Our goal is not to train a new tool-calling model, but to quantify drift sensitivity and test whether a compact inference-time repair layer can recover reliability without retraining.
paragraphs.zh: 我们将此问题视为接口漂移：即部署后工具接口发生的良性、语义保留的变化。 我们的目标不是训练一个新的工具调用模型，而是量化漂移敏感性，并测试一个紧凑的推理时修复层是否能够在无需重新训练的情况下恢复可靠性。

paragraphs.en: We instantiate drift with three deployment-motivated synthetic perturbations: (i) stale description examples that mention legacy field names, (ii) schema renaming, and (iii) distractor tools. Our primary evaluation uses Qwen3.5-9B on a 300-example DICE-BENCH slice [ 5 ] and a 200-example BFCL slice [ 21 ] under a deployment-realistic non-oracle repair protocol. Earlier oracle-constrained sweeps on additional open models are retained only as upper-bound context and for secondary analyses.
paragraphs.zh: 我们通过三种源于实际部署需求的合成扰动来具体化漂移现象：(i) 提及旧有字段名称的陈旧描述示例，(ii) 模式重命名，以及 (iii) 干扰性工具。 我们的主要评估在部署场景下真实的非神谕修复协议框架内，使用 Qwen3.5-9B 模型对包含 300 个示例的 DICE-BENCH 切片 [ 5 ] 和包含 200 个示例的 BFCL 切片 [ 21 ] 进行测试。 先前在额外开放模型上进行的受神谕约束的扫描结果仅作为上限参考背景，并用于次要分析。

paragraphs.en: This paper makes three empirical contributions, demonstrated primarily on Qwen3.5-9B with a supporting replication on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B:

paragraphs.en: Non-oracle inference-time repair recovers drift-induced failures on the primary model. On Qwen3.5-9B, SchemaShield-Lite raises DICE-300 accuracy from 0.717 0.717 to 0.813 0.813 and BFCL-200 accuracy from 0.580 0.580 to 0.805 0.805 , while showing no observed repair harms on the originally-correct slice in either benchmark. A same-protocol BFCL replication on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B ( 0.635 → 0.845 0.635\rightarrow 0.845 ) confirms the effect is not confined to a single model size, though the cleanest non-oracle evidence remains within the Qwen family.
paragraphs.zh: 非神谕推理时修复能够恢复主模型因漂移而引发的故障。 在 Qwen3.5-9B 上，SchemaShield-Lite 将 DICE-300 的准确率从 0.717 提升至 0.813，并将 BFCL-200 的准确率从 0.580 提升至 0.805，同时在两个基准测试中均未观察到对原本正确切片造成任何修复损害。 在 Qwen3.5-35B-A3B 上采用相同协议的 BFCL 复制（0.635 → 0.845）证实了这一效果并非局限于单一模型规模，尽管最清晰的非神谕证据仍存在于 Qwen 系列模型中。

paragraphs.en: Recent work has established that tool interfaces are not neutral wrappers around tool use; they are part of the learning and inference problem itself. Guo et al. [ 4 ] show that rewriting tool descriptions can substantially improve agent reliability, especially when candidate tool sets are large. Faghih et al. [ 2 ] show the opposite direction: small edits to tool descriptions can dramatically shift tool preference, exposing a fragility in description-mediated tool use. Rabinovich and Anaby-Tavor [ 14 ] study robustness in agentic function calling under toolkit changes and other perturbations, while our focus is narrower: post-deployment interface drift with fixed underlying tool semantics.

paragraphs.en: Our repair stack also connects to structured-output enforcement via constrained decoding. Grammar-constrained and grammar-aligned decoding study how to guarantee or preserve valid structured outputs during generation [ 3 , 11 ] . We instead study post-hoc validation and repair after the base model has already produced a drifted tool call. Feeding error feedback back into the prompt also relates to judge-guided prompt refinement, which improves reliability without weight updates but has clear boundary conditions [ 1 ] ; in our setting, the feedback comes from deterministic schema validation rather than an LLM judge.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的修复堆栈还通过受约束解码与结构化输出执行机制相连接。 语法约束和语法对齐的解码方法旨在研究如何在生成过程中保证或保留有效的结构化输出 [ 3 , 11 ] 。 我们转而研究在基础模型已经生成了偏离预期的工具调用之后，如何进行事后验证与修复。 将错误反馈重新输入提示词也与判官引导的提示词优化相关：这种方法无需更新权重即可提升可靠性，但存在明确的边界条件 [ 1 ] ；在我们的设定中，反馈来自确定性的模式验证，而非 LLM 判官。

sents.en: Our repair stack also connects to structured-output enforcement via constrained decoding.
sents.zh: 我们的修复堆栈还通过受约束解码与结构化输出执行机制相连接。

sents.en: Grammar-constrained and grammar-aligned decoding study how to guarantee or preserve valid structured outputs during generation [ 3 , 11 ] .

sents.en: We instead study post-hoc validation and repair after the base model has already produced a drifted tool call.

sents.en: Feeding error feedback back into the prompt also relates to judge-guided prompt refinement, which improves reliability without weight updates but has clear boundary conditions [ 1 ] ; in our setting, the feedback comes from deterministic schema validation rather than an LLM judge.

paragraphs.en: Benchmark work has also highlighted that realistic function calling is still far from solved. ComplexFuncBench introduces multi-step and constrained long-context function calling [ 25 ] , while DICE-BENCH focuses on multi-round, multi-party dialogues with tool-related information dispersed across conversation turns [ 5 ] . Other benchmarks, including API-Bank, τ \tau -bench, and ToolSandbox, similarly stress planning, state, and interaction in tool-use settings [ 7 , 22 , 9 ] . We evaluate on both DICE-BENCH and the Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (BFCL) [ 21 ] because they capture complementary settings: DICE-BENCH exercises conversational multi-turn dialogues, while BFCL tests single-turn tool calls across diverse APIs.
paragraphs.zh: 基准研究也表明，实现逼真的函数调用仍然远未解决。 ComplexFuncBench 引入了多步骤且受约束的长上下文函数调用 [ 25 ]，而 DICE-BENCH 则专注于多轮、多方对话，其中与工具相关的信息分散在对话的各个回合中 [ 5 ]。 其他基准测试，包括 API-Bank、τ \tau -bench 和 ToolSandbox，同样强调了工具使用场景中的规划、状态和交互 [ 7 , 22 , 9 ]。 我们在 DICE-BENCH 和伯克利函数调用排行榜（BFCL）[ 21 ] 上进行了评估，因为它们涵盖了互补的场景：DICE-BENCH 考察对话中的多轮互动，而 BFCL 则测试跨多种 API 的单轮工具调用。

paragraphs.en: Original : inference on the original tool interface.

paragraphs.zh: 我们的核心问题是：推理时的修复层是否能够在不损害原本正确的示例的前提下，恢复从“原始”到“漂移后”所损失的性能。

paragraphs.en: Each tool is rendered into a compact canonical form containing the tool name, description, required fields, and field-level type information. This normalizes interface presentation across tools and emphasizes current field names.
paragraphs.zh: 每个工具都被转换为一种紧凑的标准形式，其中包含工具名称、描述、必填字段以及字段级别的类型信息。 这统一了不同工具的界面呈现方式，并突出了当前的字段名称。

paragraphs.en: After the base model emits a tool call, a validator checks tool name, required fields, and argument structure. Validation produces a structured error report rather than a binary failure signal.
paragraphs.zh: 基础模型发出工具调用后，验证器会检查工具名称、必填字段和参数结构。 验证过程会生成一份结构化错误报告，而非简单的失败信号。

sents.en: After the base model emits a tool call, a validator checks tool name, required fields, and argument structure.
sents.zh: 基础模型发出工具调用后，验证器会检查工具名称、必填字段和参数结构。

paragraphs.en: If the drifted call is invalid, the model receives a repair prompt containing the task context, canonical tool card, invalid call, and validation errors. In the primary non-oracle protocol, repair proceeds in two stages. If the base call names a visible tool, validation runs against that tool and a constrained repair call is issued for that same visible tool. If the base call omits the tool name, we first run a candidate-set retry over the visible tools to produce a concrete tool call; once a visible tool is resolved, a second repair call may be constrained to that selected tool. Where provider support allows it, this second step uses forced-tool repair ; otherwise we fall back to unconstrained tool calling or JSON repair.
paragraphs.zh: 如果漂移调用无效，模型将收到一个修复提示，其中包含任务上下文、标准工具卡、无效调用以及验证错误。 在主要非神谕协议中，修复过程分为两个阶段。 如果基础调用指定了一个可见工具，则针对该工具执行验证，并为同一可见工具发出受约束的修复调用。 如果基础调用未指定工具名称，我们首先对可见工具集进行候选重试，以生成具体的工具调用；一旦确定某个可见工具，第二次修复调用即可被约束至该选定的工具。 在提供商支持允许的情况下，此第二步使用强制工具修复；否则，我们将回退到无约束工具调用或 JSON 修复。

paragraphs.en: As our component ablation in Section 6.5 shows, it is the combination of structured validation errors and tool-constrained repair that does the heavy lifting once a visible target tool has been resolved. The canonical card is useful at the initial prediction step as drift-prevention prompting, but contributes negligibly to repair-stage recovery in our oracle-constrained upper-bound ablations.
paragraphs.zh: 正如我们在第 6.5 节中的组件消融分析所示，一旦确定了可见的目标工具，结构化验证错误与工具约束修复的结合才是发挥主要作用的关键。 在初始预测阶段，标准卡片可作为防止偏移的提示而发挥作用，但在我们受预言机约束的上界消融分析中，它对修复阶段的恢复贡献微乎其微。

paragraphs.en: Three implementation details turned out to matter materially:
paragraphs.zh: 有三个实现细节被证明至关重要：

paragraphs.en: The repair prompt explicitly instructs the model to infer all required fields from the dialogue even when the invalid call is empty.
paragraphs.zh: 修复提示明确指示模型，即使无效调用为空，也应从对话中推断出所有必要字段。

paragraphs.en: When the invalid call omits the tool name, a candidate-set retry over the visible tools is needed before tool-constrained repair can fire.
paragraphs.zh: 当无效调用省略了工具名称时，在触发受工具约束的修复之前，需要对可见的工具进行候选集重试。

paragraphs.en: The repair stage uses a larger token budget than the base prediction stage. Raising repair capacity from the earlier default to 512 512 tokens fixed truncated repair outputs on longer DICE dialogues.
paragraphs.zh: 修复阶段的令牌预算比基础预测阶段更大。 将修复能力从之前的默认值提升至 512×512 个令牌，从而在较长的 DICE 对话中固定截断修复输出。

paragraphs.en: Each benchmark example is evaluated in three stages: Original, Drifted, and Repaired. Drift is injected once, the gold call is re-expressed in the renamed schema before scoring, and repair fires only when validation flags the drifted call as invalid. We average the three per-example correctness indicators over the benchmark slice to obtain the headline accuracies.
paragraphs.zh: 每个基准测试示例都分为三个阶段进行评估：原始阶段、漂移阶段和修复阶段。 漂移仅注入一次，在评分前，黄金调用会在新命名的模式中重新表达，而修复仅在验证将漂移后的调用标记为无效时触发。 我们对基准测试切片中每个示例的三个正确性指标取平均值，从而得出主要准确率。

paragraphs.en: For DICE main runs, we use mild severity: two description modes (legacy-example and marketing), two schema modes (rename-parameters and reorder-parameters), and one distractor tool. For BFCL we use medium severity: three description modes, three schema modes, and three distractors, reflecting a more aggressive drift scenario. These operators are author-designed and deployment-motivated rather than mined from real API changelogs; we return to that limitation in Section 8 . To sanity-check ecological validity, we manually audited 11 11 official changelog items from Notion and Stripe spanning 2022–2026. Six map directly to our documentation/example and parameter/schema operators, three more are close candidate-set analogues where vendors add or consolidate neighboring tools or endpoints, and two are larger structural refactors outside our semantics-preserving scope [ 10 , 17 , 18 , 20 , 19 ] . We therefore treat the synthetic operators as a compact model of common surface-form churn rather than as a measured distribution over all API evolution events.

paragraphs.en: We use two repair protocols. Our primary protocol is non-oracle and is the main evidence in this paper: the validator checks the model-selected visible tool, and when the model omits the tool name, a candidate-set retry over only the visible tools resolves a target before repair. For broader model coverage and component ablations, we also retain earlier oracle-constrained upper-bound sweeps in which the repair stage is given the benchmark target tool. These upper-bound runs remain useful for cross-model context and ablation, but they are not the paper’s deployment-facing evidence.
paragraphs.zh: 我们使用两种修复协议。 我们的主要协议是非神谕协议，也是本文的主要证据：验证器会检查模型选定的可见工具；当模型省略工具名称时，仅对可见工具进行候选集重试，即可在修复前确定目标。 为了覆盖更广泛的模型并开展组件消融分析，我们还保留了早期的神谕约束上限扫描实验，在这些实验中，修复阶段会被提供基准目标工具。 这些上限运行对于跨模型上下文和消融分析仍然有用，但它们并非本文面向部署的主要证据。

paragraphs.en: All reported results come from fixed benchmark slices, fixed drift configurations, and fixed random seeds. paragraphs.en: We therefore focus our interpretation on the large repaired-vs-drifted gaps, not on small differences between nearby runs. The bootstrap intervals in Table 1 support the main claim that structured repair helps, but they do not justify strong claims about minor oracle-vs-non-oracle differences. Paired exact McNemar tests on the final non-oracle runs also support the main repair effect: repaired beats drifted with p = 3.7 × 10 − 9 p=3.7\times 10^{-9} on DICE and p = 5.7 × 10 − 14 p=5.7\times 10^{-14} on BFCL. On shared examples, the repaired-score difference between the oracle upper bound and the final non-oracle protocol is itself not significant on either benchmark (DICE exact McNemar p = 0.125 p=0.125 ; BFCL p = 0.754 p=0.754 ), which is consistent with the small raw score gaps in Table 1 .

paragraphs.en: A first-order alternative explanation is that repair works simply because the model gets a second attempt. We test this with two baselines (Table 2 ). Naive retry re-runs the identical drifted prompt with no new information. Tool-list re-prompt tells the model the call was invalid and lists the available tool names, but provides no canonical card, no validation errors, and no view of the invalid call. This second baseline isolates whether simply flagging the error and listing tools explains the gains.
paragraphs.zh: 一种一阶的替代解释是，修复之所以有效，仅仅是因为模型获得了第二次尝试的机会。 我们通过两种基线方法对此进行了测试（表 2）。 简单的重试会重新运行完全相同的漂移提示，但不会提供任何新信息。 工具列表重提示会告知模型调用无效，并列出可用的工具名称，但不会提供标准卡片、验证错误信息或无效调用的视图。 这种第二种基线方法旨在确定，是否仅仅通过标记错误并列出工具就能解释性能的提升。

paragraphs.en: This result qualifies a common framing in the interface-drift literature. On this Qwen3.5-9B DICE-300 ablation, minor description rewording and semantics-preserving parameter renames do not meaningfully degrade accuracy; the model is evidently robust to this class of surface perturbation. The observed failure mode is candidate-set confusion : when a distractor tool with an overlapping description is added to the candidate set, tool selection degrades. In this slice, the practical implication is that tool-catalog growth deserves closer monitoring than minor description or schema revisions.

paragraphs.en: To isolate which parts of the repair stack matter once a target tool has already been resolved, Table 5 evaluates three variants of SchemaShield-Lite in an oracle-constrained upper-bound setting on both DICE-300 and BFCL-200 with Qwen3.5-9B: (i) canonical card only, where the card is prepended to the initial prompt but no validation/repair is applied; (ii) validation-plus-retry, which uses validation errors in a repair prompt but omits the canonical tool card from the repair context; and (iii) full SchemaShield-Lite (card + validation + repair).

paragraphs.en: Within this oracle-constrained setting, the BFCL rows confirm and strengthen the DICE finding in three ways. Second, the card-only configuration still never triggers the validator and recovers zero drift-induced failures, because its valid-but-imperfect outputs pass schema checking without entering the repair path. Third, validation-plus-retry without the canonical card at repair time reaches a higher repaired accuracy on BFCL than the full pipeline ( 0.820 0.820 vs 0.795 0.795 , and 26 / 34 26/34 recoveries vs 23 / 35 23/35 ), matching the pattern observed on DICE where validation-only nearly ties the full pipeline.

paragraphs.en: The pattern is consistent across models: nearly all unrecovered examples involve the repair call selecting the correct tool with well-formed arguments whose string values disagree with gold only by formatting or paraphrase. On Qwen3.5-35B ( 5 5 unrecovered), these include one strict whitespace/punctuation difference (“ the quick brown fox… ” vs “ The quick brown fox…. ”) and three enum-format or paraphrase-level mismatches (e.g. regular_season vs regular season , the office vs Office ); a single genuine failure has an empty arguments object after repair. On Llama-4-Scout ( 4 4 unrecovered), all four are format-level: ISO -prefixed dates vs two-field dates (e.g. 2023-11-10 vs 11-10 ), or JSON with quoted-number string values rather than numeric literals. On Mistral-24B ( 4 4 unrecovered), the misses include near-synonym topics ( inspirational vs inspiration , AI vs artificial intelligence , Google vs GOOGL ) and one wrong numeric amount. Across 13 unrecovered cases in total, only 2 2 are genuine inference failures (empty arguments and one wrong value); the remaining 11 11 are strict-match artifacts rather than true drift failures. The practical implication is that the paper’s reported recovery rates are a lower bound: a lenient evaluator would count most of the unrecovered cases as correct.

paragraphs.en: Our results support three narrower conclusions than the original SchemaShield-Lite framing suggested. First, non-oracle inference-time repair is a viable robustness layer for tool-calling systems under interface drift: on Qwen3.5-9B it improves over drifted performance on both DICE and BFCL while showing no observed repair harms on the originally-correct slice. Second, the main non-oracle bottleneck is missing tool names; a candidate-set retry over the visible tools closes much of the gap to the oracle upper bound. Third, on our DICE-300 primary-model ablation, candidate-set drift is a more important failure mode than description or schema drift.

paragraphs.en: Together these findings simplify the deployment picture. A practitioner does not need a heavy per-tool canonicalization pipeline; a visible-tool validator, a candidate-set retry for missing tool names, and a constrained repair call once a tool is resolved already recover most of the damage we observe. And the monitoring story is clearer: in our slices, tool-catalog expansion appears more consequential than minor description or parameter rename churn. The additional BFCL-200 Qwen3.5-35B-A3B replication suggests this practical recipe is not limited to one exact model size, even if broader cross-family evidence remains thin.

paragraphs.en: These same results also matter for adversarial interface manipulation. Faghih et al. [ 2 ] show that small description edits can steer tool selection even when semantics are unchanged. Our ablation suggests that the more serious surface to monitor is not just description wording in isolation, but the combination of description overlap and candidate-set expansion: once distractor tools enter the visible set, routing degrades quickly. In that sense, the non-oracle validator-plus-repair stack is relevant not only to benign interface drift but also to description-surface attacks that aim to induce tool confusion.

paragraphs.en: Several limitations remain. First, although we now include a strong BFCL non-oracle replication on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and a weaker portability check on Llama-4-Scout, the cleanest successful non-oracle evidence is still concentrated in the Qwen3.5 family; the broader multi-model results retained in the paper remain mostly oracle-constrained upper bounds rather than full non-oracle replications. Second, the BFCL evaluation now covers three open-model non-oracle runs, but two are Qwen3.5-family results and the third is materially bottlenecked by missing tool names; we also include one closed-model BFCL sanity check, but not yet a broader closed-model sweep. Third, our drift operators focus on stale descriptions, renamed fields, and distractors; other forms of interface drift (for example, type narrowing, enum replacement, or multi-tool refactors) remain untested, and although we now add a small manual audit of official vendor changelogs, the perturbations are still author-designed rather than mined from a larger empirical change distribution. Fourth, the drift-type and component ablations remain oracle-constrained upper bounds, so their mechanism-level conclusions may not fully transfer when non-oracle tool resolution fails. Fifth, evaluation uses hosted inference and so may incorporate provider-specific tool-calling behavior. Sixth, the “repair > > original” effect indicates that SchemaShield-Lite is also patching baseline failures, useful in deployment, but a complication for clean attribution to drift recovery specifically. Seventh, strict string-matching against gold calls undercounts true recoveries: manual inspection of the 13 13 unrecovered cases on the three non-primary models (Section 6.6 ) shows that 11 11 are formatting or paraphrase artifacts, so the reported recovery rates should be read as lower bounds. Finally, while we now report broader cross-protocol significance for oracle-vs-non-oracle repaired outcomes on the shared Qwen slices, we still lack a broader wall-clock latency sweep across benchmarks, providers, and models.

paragraphs.en: We studied SchemaShield-Lite, a lightweight inference-time validation-and-repair stack for tool calling under interface drift. On Qwen3.5-9B under a non-oracle candidate-retry protocol, SchemaShield-Lite improves DICE-300 from 0.717 0.717 to 0.813 0.813 and BFCL-200 from 0.580 0.580 to 0.805 0.805 , with no observed repair harms on the originally-correct slice in both benchmarks. Three findings qualify the picture. A naive-retry baseline does not explain the gains. Description and schema drift cause only small degradations on our DICE slice, while candidate-set drift is the dominant failure mode. And in the non-oracle setting, missing tool names are the main repair bottleneck: a candidate-set retry over the visible tools substantially reduces unresolved cases and closes most of the gap to oracle-constrained upper bounds. Additional oracle-constrained sweeps across other models and upper-bound ablations remain useful context, and a BFCL sanity check on GPT-4o-mini suggests that stronger closed models suffer less drift damage to begin with. A same-protocol BFCL-200 replication on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B ( 0.635 → 0.845 0.635\rightarrow 0.845 ) materially strengthens the main claim, but the cleanest successful non-oracle evidence is still concentrated in the Qwen family. The paper should therefore be read as a controlled study of drift sensitivity and inference-time repair rather than as a complete account of production interface drift.
